system.name: Joplin
system.description: A free, open-source note-taking and to-do application that keeps notes on each device, synchronises them through a sync service of the user's choice with optional end-to-end encryption, and comes with a web clipper, plugins, and Joplin Server for synchronisation, sharing and publishing.

corpus.included: The whole repository github.com/laurent22/joplin at branch dev and its history since 2026-05-25 (blobless clone, read only): the apps, the shared library, Joplin Server, the Transcribe server, the plugin tools, the website sources and the documentation in readme/.
corpus.excluded: Dependencies: the vendored forks packages/fork-htmlparser2, packages/fork-sax, packages/fork-uslug, packages/turndown, packages/turndown-plugin-gfm, packages/react-native-alarm-notification and packages/react-native-saf-x, the vendored whisper.cpp copy in packages/whisper-voice-typing/vendor, the third-party scripts in packages/lib/vendor and packages/renderer/vendor, the clipper's Readability files, the root bootstrap.bundle.min.js and the bundled Yarn release. Generated output such as lockfiles. No secrets were found: the .env-sample files hold placeholders.

consumers.name: Note taker
consumers.description: A person who writes, organises, finds and keeps notes and to-dos on their own devices, synchronises and encrypts them, clips web pages, shares notebooks and publishes notes, directly or through scripts and AI apps they connect.

consumers.name: Plugin developer
consumers.description: A person who writes plugins that add features to the desktop and mobile apps and publishes them for other users to install.

consumers.name: Server administrator
consumers.description: A person who runs a Joplin Server for themselves or an organisation and manages its users and maintenance from its admin pages.

consumers.name: Published-note reader
consumers.description: Anyone who opens the link of a published note in a browser, without an account.

providers.name: Joplin apps
providers.description: The note-taking apps for desktop, mobile, web and terminal, which keep the notes on each device and share one back end.

parts.name: Desktop, mobile, web and terminal front ends
parts.why: Clients that present the shared back end's capabilities, each with its own UI framework (readme/dev/spec/architecture.md); they are the desktop, mobile, web and terminal app interfaces.

parts.name: Web clipper extension
parts.why: A client that captures a page and posts it to the Data API (packages/app-clipper/popup/src/bridge.js); part of the web clipper interface.

parts.name: Data API and MCP server
parts.why: Request handlers that pass calls on to the models, the search engine, the revision service and the AI tools (packages/lib/services/rest/routes, packages/lib/services/mcp/McpServer.ts); they are interfaces.

parts.name: Shared front-end code
parts.why: Screens, commands, keymaps and reducers used by several front ends (packages/lib/components, packages/lib/commands, packages/lib/services/CommandService.ts); a library of the interfaces.

parts.name: Note editors and PDF viewer
parts.why: UI libraries embedded by the front ends (packages/editor, packages/pdf-viewer).

parts.name: Note renderer
parts.why: A library that turns Markdown or HTML into HTML for the apps and the server, keeping no state (packages/renderer).

parts.name: Utilities
parts.why: Libraries such as packages/utils, the shim, path and string helpers, and the whiteboard format in packages/lib/services/whiteboard.

parts.name: Joplin Server API client
parts.why: An adapter to Joplin Server's REST API (packages/lib/JoplinServerApi.ts) used by the Synchroniser, Sharing, OCR and the Joplin Cloud AI provider.

components.name: Note collection
components.description: Keeps the notes, notebooks, tags, attachments, chat conversations and settings in the local database and attachment folder, and is the only way other parts read or change them.

parts.name: Item models
parts.why: Note, Folder, Tag, NoteTag, Resource, NoteResource, ItemChange and the other models change each other's records (Folder.delete deletes notes, Note.save writes ItemChange), so they form this component rather than components of their own.

parts.name: Trash and attachment bookkeeping
parts.why: services/trash and services/ResourceService.ts change notes, notebooks and attachments through the same models; part of this component.

parts.name: Database, migrations and settings
parts.why: Storage: JoplinDatabase.ts, services/database, models/Setting.ts and services/KvStore.ts are how the component keeps things.

components.name: Synchroniser
components.description: Decides what to upload, download and delete between the device and the sync target, resolves conflicts, keeps the sync info and locks the target while it works.

parts.name: Sync target drivers
parts.why: Adapters to the outside services, variants of the FileApi driver contract registered in SyncTargetRegistry (packages/lib/file-api.ts, file-api-driver-*.ts, SyncTarget*.ts).

components.name: Sync engine
components.description: Runs the sync steps (upload, delete, delta, conflict handling, target upgrade and attachment downloads) and keeps the sync info and sync times.

serves.area: Keep the lock key with the sync target
Keep keys with the sync target

parts.name: Migration handler
parts.why: Writes the target's info.json directly as well as through syncInfoUtils (MigrationHandler.ts), the same record the sync loop writes, so it is part of the sync engine.

parts.name: Attachment fetcher
parts.why: ResourceFetcher.ts shares the attachment download states with the sync steps (syncDeleteStep.ts and handleConflictAction.ts call Resource.setLocalState), so it is part of the sync engine.

parts.name: Conflict merge and upload helpers
parts.why: services/conflict and ItemUploader.ts are libraries and steps the sync loop calls in-process.

parts.name: Sync status report
parts.why: services/ReportService.ts presents the sync state on the status screen; part of the interfaces' use of the engine.

parts.name: Sync scheduler
parts.why: registry.ts scheduleSync and setupRecurrentSync only decide when to call Synchronizer.start; the entry point of this component.

components.name: Lock handler
components.description: Writes and removes the sync locks on the target and decides when a lock is active or expired, so two clients do not upgrade the target at once.

components.name: Encryption
components.description: Holds the decrypted encryption keys, encrypts and decrypts items and files, and decrypts downloaded items in the background.

parts.name: Public-private key pairs
parts.why: A library of key-pair functions (services/e2ee/ppk); the pair itself is kept in the sync info.

parts.name: Master password storage
parts.why: The master password is kept as a secure setting, which the note collection stores through the operating system's keychain adapter (services/keychain); not part of this component.

components.name: Encryption service
components.description: Holds the loaded master keys and encrypts and decrypts strings and files with them, creates keys and checks master passwords.

parts.name: Platform crypto
parts.why: Adapters to each platform's crypto (services/e2ee/crypto.ts, cryptoShared.ts).

parts.name: Enable and disable flows
parts.why: Functions in services/e2ee/utils.ts that change settings and the sync info around the service; part of it.

components.name: Decryption worker
components.description: Decrypts items that arrived encrypted, in the background, and records the ones that keep failing.

components.name: Search engine
components.description: Keeps a full-text index of the notes and their attachments' text and answers keyword searches with ranked results.

parts.name: Query parsing
parts.why: Libraries (filterParser.ts, queryBuilder.ts, gotoAnythingStyleQuery.ts) used by the one indexing and querying class.

components.name: Note history
components.description: Saves earlier versions of changed notes at intervals, rebuilds them from patches and restores them.

components.name: Plugin service
components.description: Installs, loads, runs, updates and removes plugins, keeps their state, and carries out what plugins ask through the plugin API.

parts.name: View and menu controllers
parts.why: WebviewController.ts and the menu and toolbar controllers change the same plugin state as PluginService.ts (reducer.ts), so they belong to this component.

parts.name: Plugin runners
parts.why: Host plugin code in a sandbox per platform and relay its calls (BasePluginRunner.ts, app-desktop/services/plugins/PluginRunner.ts); not components.

parts.name: Repository client
parts.why: An adapter to the plugin repository (RepositoryApi.ts).

parts.name: Plugin API
parts.why: The `joplin` object (services/plugins/api) passes plugins' calls on to the app's services; the plugin API interface.

parts.name: Default plugins and blocked versions
parts.why: defaultPlugins/** installs the bundled plugins and refreshBlockedPluginVersions.ts fetches versions not to run, both through PluginService's state; part of this component.

components.name: Sharing
components.description: Shares notebooks and publishes notes through Joplin Server, keeps the shares and invitations, and handles invitation responses.

parts.name: Invitation responses and share state
parts.why: invitationRespond.ts and reducer.ts work on the same share state as ShareService.ts: one store, one component.

components.name: AI
components.description: Answers chat requests through the chat model the user chose, and keeps an on-device index of note meanings for semantic search.

parts.name: Chat providers
parts.why: Adapters to outside chat services, variants of ChatProviderBase (services/ai/providers).

components.name: AI chat
components.description: Picks the chat provider, refuses remote providers unless allowed, counts tokens, runs the chat panel's requests and the note tools used by the chat panel and the MCP server.

parts.name: Note tools
parts.why: services/ai/tools relay note operations to the note collection and the search engine for the chat panel and the MCP server.

parts.name: Chat panel requests
parts.why: noteChat.ts builds the chat panel's request from the open note or selection and applies the reply's edits; part of this component.

components.name: Semantic index
components.description: Computes and stores note embeddings in the background with a local model and finds notes by meaning.

parts.name: Indexer and search
parts.why: EmbeddingIndexer.ts writes the index and SearchService.ts reads it through the same model (models/NoteEmbedding.ts): one store.

parts.name: Local model runtime and download
parts.why: Adapters (LocalEmbeddingProvider.ts, EmbeddingModelDownloader.ts) and a library (chunker.ts).

components.name: OCR
components.description: Scans images and PDF attachments in the background to extract their text, locally or through Joplin Server's handwriting transcription.

parts.name: OCR drivers
parts.why: Adapters, variants of OcrDriverBase: OcrDriverTesseract.ts runs the local engine, OcrDriverTranscribe.ts calls Joplin Server.

parts.name: Accessible PDF and text filters
parts.why: Libraries (services/ocr/utils).

components.name: Import and export
components.description: Turns files from other apps and formats into notes, and notes into files, through a registry of import and export modules that plugins can extend.

components.name: Format registry
components.description: Keeps the list of import and export modules, including those plugins register, and runs the right one for each request.

components.name: Importers
components.description: Read ENEX, Markdown, Markdown with front matter, OneNote, Obsidian, JEX and raw files and create notes, notebooks, tags and attachments from them; variants of one importer contract.

parts.name: OneNote converter
parts.why: A library in Rust compiled for the OneNote importer (packages/onenote-converter).

components.name: Exporters
components.description: Write notes and notebooks as JEX, raw, Markdown, HTML or PDF files; variants of one exporter contract.

parts.name: HTML packer
parts.why: A library that packs an HTML file and its resources into one file (packages/htmlpack).

components.name: Alarms
components.description: Schedules and clears the notifications of to-dos with a due date through the operating system.

parts.name: Notification drivers
parts.why: Adapters to the operating system's notifications (AlarmServiceDriverNode.ts, app-mobile/services/AlarmServiceDriver.*.ts).

components.name: Note lock
components.description: Locks chosen notes with a separate password, keeps the lock key and the unlocked session, and re-encrypts locked notes when the key changes.

parts.name: Lock operations
parts.why: setNoteLockState.ts, bulkSetNoteLockState.ts, NoteLockKeyMigration.ts and NoteLockService.ts lock, unlock and re-encrypt notes through the Note model with the session's key, relaying crypto to the Encryption service.

parts.name: Prompts
parts.why: UI helpers (noteLockPrompts.ts).

components.name: Lock key
components.description: Creates, resets, re-encrypts and opens the note lock key.

components.name: Unlock session
components.description: Holds the decrypted lock key while the user has unlocked locked notes, and refuses to unlock during a key reset or migration.

components.name: Profiles
components.description: Keeps the list of profiles on the device and which settings are shared between them.

providers.name: Joplin Server
providers.description: The synchronisation server, self-hosted or run as Joplin Cloud, that stores the apps' items and lets users share notebooks, publish notes and manage their accounts.

parts.name: Routes and views
parts.why: HTTP handlers and templates that pass requests on to the models and services (packages/server/src/routes, views); they are the server's interfaces.

parts.name: Published-note rendering
parts.why: utils/joplinUtils.ts and renderMarkdown.ts render a shared note with the note renderer for the published note page; part of that interface.

parts.name: Server framework
parts.why: Configuration, environment, middleware and utilities shared by the server's parts (app.ts, config.ts, env.ts, middleware, utils).

components.name: Server store
components.description: Keeps accounts, items, changes, shares, sessions, notifications, subscriptions, emails and sync locks in the server database and content storage.

parts.name: Content storage drivers
parts.why: Storage: database, filesystem, memory and S3 drivers, variants of StorageDriverBase (models/items/storage).

parts.name: Login and payment adapters
parts.why: Adapters to the organisation's directory and identity provider and to Stripe (utils/ldapLogin.ts, utils/saml.ts, utils/stripe.ts), called by the account models.

components.name: Accounts and items
components.description: Keeps users, sessions, items, changes, shares, share users, notifications, applications, subscriptions, queued emails and user deletions, whose models change each other's records.

parts.name: Item, change and share models
parts.why: ItemModel, ChangeModel, UserItemModel, ShareModel and ShareUserModel write each other's records.

parts.name: Account models
parts.why: UserModel writes sessions, tokens, recovery codes, notifications, items and shares; SubscriptionModel and UserFlagModel write users.

components.name: Sync locks
components.description: Grants, lists and releases the sync locks clients hold on their account's data.

components.name: Task service
components.description: Runs the server's maintenance tasks on their schedules or on demand and records their state and last runs.

parts.name: Email sender
parts.why: An adapter run by the ProcessEmails task that sends queued emails through SMTP (services/EmailService.ts).

parts.name: User deletion processing
parts.why: The implementation of the ProcessUserDeletions task (services/UserDeletionService.ts).

components.name: Transcribe server
components.description: A separate server that reads handwriting in images with a local language model, one job at a time, for Joplin Server.

parts.name: API, job queue and job processor
parts.why: The API creates jobs and the processor updates them in the same queue (transcribe/src/services/queue, workers/JobProcessor.ts): one store, one component.

parts.name: Handwriting engine call
parts.why: Runs the local recognition engine (transcribe/src/core/HtrCli.ts): an implementation choice.

providers.name: Plugin repository
providers.description: The public list of plugins at github.com/joplin/plugins, built from npm packages by the repository builder, from which the apps install plugins.

parts.name: Build command
parts.why: Searches npm, validates and copies each plugin and writes the manifests and the README (plugin-repo-cli/index.ts commandBuild).

parts.name: Release command
parts.why: Uploads the built archives to a release of the same repository (commands/updateRelease.ts); writes the same store as the build command.

parts.name: Local publish command
parts.why: Publishes a plugin to a local registry for testing (index.ts commandPublishPlugin); a development aid.

questions.question: Is Joplin Server a provider of its own at Level 1, or part of one Joplin system?
questions.answer: A provider of its own rather than a component of one system provider; it has its own deployment (Dockerfile.server, the Docker image), its own data (users, items, shares) and consumers of its own (administrators, published-note readers), and users choose it knowingly as Joplin Cloud or a sync target, but the apps cannot share or publish without it, so one could also read it as the apps' back end.

questions.question: Is the plugin repository a provider, part of the apps, or engineering tooling?
questions.answer: A Level 1 provider for plugin developers rather than tooling or a component of the apps; it has its own repository, data (manifests.json and archives) and consumer, and it decides which packages may publish under which ID, but it runs as a scheduled build in another repository, which makes it look like tooling.

questions.question: Are the Data API's scripts and the AI apps connected through MCP separate consumers?
questions.answer: Interfaces of the note taker's boundary rather than consumers of their own; the model treats what consumers run for themselves as another interface, and both are reached with the user's own token, but readme/api/index.md frames the Data API as 'for external applications', which could be partner apps with goals of their own.

questions.question: Is the web clipper an interface or a provider?
questions.answer: An interface of the apps rather than a provider; it keeps no data and needs the desktop app's clipper service, though it ships separately in browser stores.

questions.question: Where does joplinapp.org belong?
questions.answer: An interface of Joplin Server, for its plans page that starts a Stripe checkout, rather than of the apps or an exclusion; the rest of the site is static help and news with no capability, and no rule says which provider owns a site that documents several.

questions.question: Is the note collection one component even though its models call services?
questions.answer: One component rather than several or none; the item models change each other's records and every other part reaches the database only through them (only SearchEngine and KvStore run SQL themselves), but BaseItem and Note call the encryption, share and revision services injected by BaseApplication.ts, and import synchroniser utilities (mustConfirmPlaintextUploads, syncDebugLog, syncInfoUtils), so the seam between the note collection and the synchroniser is blurred.

questions.question: Should model classes that only one service writes belong to that service?
questions.answer: To that service (Revision to Note history, Alarm to Alarms, NoteEmbedding to the semantic index, MasterKey to the encryption service) rather than to the note collection; they sit in lib/models beside the shared models, and the synchroniser also saves revisions and master keys through them when they arrive.

questions.question: Should the migration handler and the attachment fetcher be components of their own inside the synchroniser?
questions.answer: Parts of the sync engine rather than components; the migration handler writes info.json directly as the sync loop does, and the fetcher shares the attachment download states with the sync steps, though each has its own class and entry points.

questions.question: Should the note lock open into two one-class components?
questions.answer: Opened into Lock key and Unlock session rather than kept closed; each class keeps state only it changes and NoteLockKey.ts says the key must be rotated through the session, but the feature is about 600 lines and both classes keep their key in the synchroniser's sync info.

questions.question: Should import and export open into a registry, importers and exporters?
questions.answer: Opened rather than closed; modules are registered through Module.ts and plugins (registerImportModule, registerExportModule) and each family fulfils a typed base class, but the importers and exporters keep no state and work only through the note collection.

questions.question: Should each file-based sync service be its own outside service?
questions.answer: One outside service each (Dropbox, OneDrive, WebDAV server, S3 storage) rather than one 'cloud file storage'; they have separate APIs and credentials, though the synchroniser uses them all through one FileApi driver contract, which repeats the same boundaries for the synchroniser, the sync engine and the lock handler.

questions.question: Are Joplin Cloud AI and the Teams endpoints part of Joplin Server?
questions.answer: Joplin Cloud AI is an outside service rather than part of Joplin Server, because its route (api/ai/chat/completions) is not in packages/server and JoplinCloud.ts points to another repository; the same holds for api/teams, which ShareService.loadTeamUsers calls; the Teams and Email to Note features documented for Joplin Cloud are excluded as absent from the code.

questions.question: Is the server's sync lock model a component inside the server store?
questions.answer: A component (Sync locks) rather than part of Accounts and items; only LockModel writes the lock entries and they are reached only through its three methods, but it stores them in the shared key-value table through keyValue().readThenWrite, so no boundary is drawn between it and Accounts and items.

questions.question: Are calls from one component into another's helpers settled?
questions.answer: Recorded rather than modelled as boundaries: the synchroniser checks note lock state (NoteLockSession.isMigrating, NoteLockNote.isLocking, parkedNoteLockKeyInUse); the Joplin Cloud AI provider and the transcription driver borrow the sync target's API client through reg.syncTarget().fileApi().driver().api(); the raw importer decrypts locked notes with NoteLockService.withDecryptedKey and the raw exporter reads key IDs with EncryptionService.decodeHeaderString; routes/admin/tasks.ts reads task states from the model instead of the task service. Each is a check or step of the caller's own capability, but each reaches past the contract named in the map.

questions.question: Should Level 3 components have boundaries with Level 2 components of the same provider, such as the sync engine with the note collection?
questions.answer: Not drawn rather than repeated; the Level 2 boundary (Synchroniser with the note collection) already holds those capabilities, and the format only requires repeating boundaries with outside services.

questions.question: Are signing in to Joplin Server and checking the master password capabilities of the synchroniser?
questions.answer: Steps of its uploads and downloads rather than capabilities; the synchroniser would not call them if the other operations did not need them; signing in stays a capability for the note taker on the server's web pages.

questions.question: Is the Transcribe server a component of Joplin Server or a provider?
questions.answer: A component of Joplin Server rather than a provider; it has its own deployment and job store, but users only reach it through Joplin Server's api/transcribe route, which forwards with a shared secret.
